beats.say: Hello! Today we will spot the scary warnings that pop up on your screen.
A window like this wants to scare you into calling a number.
A real warning never gives you a phone number and never rushes you.
The rule is simple: do not call, close the window, force quit the browser if needed.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs that this window is a trick.

body.text: The system found four viruses and your personal data is at risk.
Do not close this window or all your files will be deleted.

spots.label: No closing allowed
spots.explain: A real system never forbids you to close a window. This is fear, meant to keep you there.

spots.label: Phone number
spots.explain: An operating system never shows a support number on screen. This number belongs to the scammer.

spots.label: Countdown
spots.explain: The timer is there to rush you. A warning that gives no time to think is fake.

scenes.title: While reading the news
scenes.intro: You are reading a news site and windows suddenly pop up. Choose the right step for each one.

body.text: There is malware on your computer. Call support now: +994 12 000 70 05

actions.label: Close the window
actions.feedback: Correct. Simply closing a window like this is the right answer.

actions.label: Call the number shown
actions.feedback: The fake agent will scare you even more. Never call this number.

actions.label: Press the Scan button
actions.feedback: That button opens another fake page. Do not touch anything in the window.

body.text: Do not turn off the computer. If you close this without support, your data will be lost.

steps.say: Now the screen is full and it is making a sound.

actions.label: Force quit the browser
actions.feedback: Correct. When you force the browser to close, this fake screen disappears too.

actions.label: Call support
actions.feedback: The sound and full screen are only there to scare you. If you call, they will try to control your device.

body.text: Restart the browser to apply the changes.

steps.say: This is the browser's own quiet notice.

actions.label: Update
actions.feedback: Correct. A real update is calm, gives no number and does not rush you.

actions.label: Later
actions.feedback: That is fine too. You can update whenever you like, there is no danger.

actions.label: Call support just in case
actions.feedback: There is no need. A simple update notice does not require calling anyone.

body.text: The problem is not solved. Call now for help.

steps.say: You closed it, but the window came back.

actions.label: Close the whole browser
actions.feedback: Correct. When you close the browser fully, these pages go away too.

actions.label: Tell tech support
actions.feedback: Good step. You can call your own tech support and ask about it.

actions.label: Call the number
actions.feedback: The window coming back is part of the trick. Do not call that number.

scenes.prompt: Match each sign to the right response.

pairs.left: A window filling the whole screen
A support number on the screen
pairs.right: A real warning gives no number
It is there to scare you

scenes.explain: All of these signs exist to scare you. Stay calm and close the window.

question.prompt: A window pops up and tells you to call a number. What is the first step?

options.label: I close the window and force quit the browser if needed
options.feedback: Correct. A warning like this is harmless and disappears when you close it.

options.label: To be safe, I call the number shown
options.feedback: That number belongs to the scammer. If you call, they will try to control your device.

options.label: I turn the computer off right away
options.feedback: There is no need. Closing the window or the browser is enough.

scenes.explain: The scary window wants to pull you into a call. Do not call, just close it.

points: Do not trust a scary window that pops up out of nowhere
Never call the number it shows
Close the window, force quit the browser if needed
